石川さん家.name: Ishikawa-san Chi
石川さん家.desc: An open-air diner loved by students, near Meio University and a nursing school. Tacos and taco rice are the main draw, but there's also "nankotsu soba," topped with hefty soft-bone pork ribs in a rich, sweetish seasoning. A community-rooted shop where the proprietress runs everything solo.
t: This time I'm introducing "Shokuji-dokoro Ishikawa-san Chi" in Biimata, Nago🏠 I ate here in March 2025😄
Ishikawa-san Chi
It's right in front of the nursing school in Nago, and Meio University is nearby too, so the shop is in an area bustling with students and young people.

As for the exterior, a signboard with an eye-catching yellow band is mounted on the ground floor of a mostly white building, with the words "Shokuji-dokoro - Tacos, Taco Rice, Soba - Ishikawa-san Chi" written big and bold inside an orange round logo.
Menu posted outside the shop

It feels less like an Okinawa soba shop and more like a diner where tacos and taco rice are the main thing, and sure enough, looking at the menu, there's a rich variety of dishes besides Okinawa soba, like taco rice, taco rice sets, cheese curry rice, salted beef tongue set meals, and pig's feet (tebichi) set meals😄
Near the entrance of the shop

Rather than an interior, it's more like tables and chairs lined up in a semi-outdoor open space with a roof over the parking area; a so-called open-air diner style. Menus with photos are posted all along the wall, and it's fun just to look at them. There's an unpretentious, very Okinawan local feel, and it has the atmosphere of a truly community-rooted diner🌺

When I visited at lunchtime, there were lots of young students, probably from the nearby schools. The proprietress running the place solo looked extremely busy handling the customers who kept coming one after another. It took a while from ordering until the food came out, so I waited😅
What I ordered this time was the "nankotsu soba (large)" for ¥900🍜
Nankotsu soba, large ¥900

First, a sip of the broth. It's a combined pork bone and bonito broth, with the pork bone flavor coming clearly to the front. It doesn't have any especially standout character, but it's just plain tasty😋
Nankotsu soba, large ¥900

Next, the noodles. They're medium-thick and straight, with an overall softish texture. Personally I'd be happier with a bit more firmness and springiness, but they blended well with the broth and were easy to eat.

And the highlight this time, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki)!🥩 Big chunky pieces were piled in generously, and visually the volume is quite something. The sweetish, rich flavor had soaked in thoroughly, and in that respect they were satisfying. However, some sinewy texture remained, and rather than being finished meltingly tender, they were finished with a chew. My impression was I'd appreciate it if they were simmered a bit longer🤔

Rating (9/15): It was a bowl that felt like "just plain tasty~." Given its location near the nursing school and Meio University, I could really see that it's loved as an everyday eatery for students. I was also curious about the other dishes like tacos and taco rice, so it might be fun to come back for those. Please consider it as one option when you're looking for an Okinawa soba shop in the Nago area😊

具志川そば 愛ちゃん.name: Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan
具志川そば 愛ちゃん.desc: An Okinawa soba specialty shop in Ota, Uruma, marked by a big red-and-yellow sign. A two-in-one shop that's a soba shop by day and a place for drinks and karaoke by night; its signature is Gushikawa soba in a light broth with plenty of bonito. Autographed cards line the walls, and it's loved by locals for everyday meals.
t: I ate here in March 2025😄 This time I went to "Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan" in Ota, Uruma😊✨
Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan
Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan
Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan

A conspicuous red-and-yellow sign sits boldly on top of a big building, so you can spot the shop right away even from a distance. It's along the road, and you can see a gas station and a convenience store across the street, so it was an easy place to find even while driving🚗 The parking is under and beside the shop, so it's quite easy to pull into. When you're making the rounds of Okinawa soba shops, places that still have this old-fashioned diner feel always catch your interest.

Near the shop entrance is a big yellow banner reading "Okinawa Soba Specialty Shop," along with a hand-drawn-style illustration of soba, giving it plenty of local feel🌺 The sign reads "Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan" in big letters, and the name alone feels friendly somehow.
Meal ticket machine

When you enter the shop, it's a style where you first buy a ticket at the meal ticket machine. Gushikawa soba, braised pork belly soba, soft-bone soba, pork offal (nakami) soba, yushi-dofu soba, soki soba, and more are lined up, and the menu was bigger than I expected🍜 This time I ordered the "Gushikawa soba, large" from among them.

Inside there are counter seats, table seats, and what look like tatami seats in the back, so it's an easy atmosphere to walk into whether you're alone or with family😊 The wooden counter is fairly wide, and it was nice to be able to eat leisurely.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Autographs of celebrities posted on the shop wall

Lots of autographed cards decorate the walls, and there was an air of "lots of different people have visited here." There are also Okinawan fabrics, awamori bottles, and drum and ship's-wheel decorations; it's an interior that isn't too flashy but properly has an Okinawan feel🌴 Rather than something elaborately built for tourists, my impression was of a relaxed soba shop where locals come to eat on a regular basis.

The "Gushikawa soba, large" that was brought out after a while looked like classic Okinawa soba🍜 A clear broth topped with braised pork belly, soft-bone-type meat, fish cake, and green onion; not flashy, but a reassuring bowl😋
Gushikawa soba, large ¥950
When I first took a sip of the broth, the bonito broth really comes through.
Gushikawa soba, large ¥950

The noodles are about medium-thin, loosely wavy noodles, and the texture was on the soft side🍜 They have the rustic simplicity of Okinawa soba, but rather than the type where you really enjoy the firmness, they're the type that slurps down easily. I felt they were a little soft here😅

The meat topping had moderate seasoning, with a balance where the sweet-savory flavor isn't too strong🥩 The soft-bone-type meat had a bit of sinewy texture, and rather than meltingly tender, it was the type that keeps a meaty texture.

Rating (9/15): Overall, the Gushikawa soba (large) at "Gushikawa Soba Ai-chan" left the impression of plainly tasty Okinawa soba that's easy for locals to have as an everyday meal, rather than a highly distinctive, memorable bowl🍜✨ With its combination of a light broth with plenty of bonito, softish medium-thin wavy noodles, and moderately seasoned meat, it has few quirks, in a good way. Personally, I have no major complaints about any of the noodles, broth, or toppings, but I think it would have been more memorable with one more step of strength that makes you go "oh!"😊

Its house-made thick noodles boiled after you order and its distinctive A set with wasabi for changing up the flavor were its specialties.

When I finally got inside and was shown to my seat, they recommended the "A set," which includes the "Suu~gii~jii soba," from the menu, so I went ahead and ordered the "A set."
The menu had an explanation of the types of noodle firmness, but I wasn't particularly asked how I wanted my noodles (^0^;)

It finally came (^0^;) First, I taste the broth. It's a combined bonito and pork bone broth, with the pork bone slightly prominent. It's tasty, but kind of ordinary😆
A set ¥1,100 (Suu~gii~jii soba, medium; jushi; small side dish)

Next, I taste the noodles. The house-made noodles are thick and straight. The menu had an explanation of noodle firmness, and I don't know whether these were "regular noodles" or "firm noodles," but while they felt a little firm, I didn't think they were as firm as at "Ishigufu," which I ate in Nago and Urasoe.

The seared braised pork belly had a sinewy texture. Also, to change up the flavor I put wasabi in the broth and tried it; it had a refreshing quality, and I thought it went surprisingly well with Okinawa soba broth. It made me want to try it when I eat Okinawa soba at home too😁
Rating (9/15): This shop closes at the end of February 2024, so you'll be eating it as "Sakihama Seimen" at its new location in Yamada, Onna Village.

I think the menu will be about the same at the new location; it's plainly tasty, but considering I waited the longest ever, it wasn't all that, I thought it was perfectly ordinary. Changing up the flavor with wasabi is something no other shop has, so if you have a chance to eat in Onna Village, why not give it a try?😄

本部そば.name: Motobu Soba
本部そば.desc: On National Route 449, marked by a yellow exterior and black 3D lettering. The famous "three-kind platter" is a meat trio of bone-in pork ribs, braised pork belly, and soft-bone pork ribs. There are also edgy dishes like Motobu-raised goat soup and goat soba. Covered terrace seating available.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 5), with some additions of my own lol I went to eat here in December 2024😄
It was a day when rain clouds made the color of the sea look just a little heavy, on the way from Nago toward Motobu. I stopped by "Motobu Soba," a shop whose yellow exterior jumps right out at you.
Motobu Soba
As you can see in the photo, the exterior displaying "Motobu Soba" in black 3D lettering really stands out, and the little shisa by the entrance seems to greet you with a "welcome!", which is cute🦁✨.
Menu posted on the building's exterior wall
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Menu posted in the shop

Inside the shop there are seashells, woodwork objects, and even houseplants; it has a relaxed atmosphere, as if a tourist-spot vibe and local everyday life were mixed exactly half and half. The wooden-placard menus lined up high on the wall are very Okinawan too, and just looking at them gets me excited.
Menu posted in the shop
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu

That day I had the "Motobu soba three-kind platter," listed first on the menu and seemingly their selling point, in regular size. As shown in the menu photo, it's ¥900 including tax, a really good value. Outside there's also a covered terrace, and raindrops were wetting the wooden floor, but I couldn't help imagining how pleasant a space it would be on a sunny day🌺.
There's outdoor seating, but unfortunately it was raining (^0^;)
Motobu soba three-kind platter (regular) ¥900

Now, the bowl arrives. Beyond the rising steam, a clear pork-bone-based broth glistens. As in the photo, green onion and fish cake are modestly placed on top, and the star meat trio is bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki)🍖. First, a sip of the broth. The aroma leads with the fullness of pork bone, but the flavor is surprisingly restrained; neither the salt nor the fat is pushy, and I think "a classic, ordinary pork bone broth" describes it perfectly.
Motobu soba three-kind platter (regular) ¥900

The noodles are medium-thin and straight. As in the noodle lift shot, they have a hint of squared edges, but they're cooked on the soft side. Rather than a springy bounce when you bite, they're the type that hugs the broth and slips down smoothly. Personally I'd like them with just half a step more firmness.
The seasoning is light overall. On the other hand, the bone-in pork ribs and braised pork belly retain a noticeable sinewiness, the kind where you enjoy the chewiness.

As shown in the photos, the menu is wide-ranging too; besides soba, it's interesting that there's taco rice, seafood rice bowls, a "greedy set," and even "tsukemen (hot/cold)." They've also got supporting dishes like mozuku seaweed in vinegar, sea grapes, and jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) well covered, which gives the reassurance of being able to tell tourists, "you can sample all the flavors of Okinawa here." The "Motobu-raised goat soup (with offal)" and "goat soba" pushed on the posters are surely things fans would make a special trip for. This sense of balance, offering edgy dishes like these while keeping the everyday soba basic, may be the reason for this shop's popularity👍.

When I finished eating and glanced outside, the rain was still falling finely, but the yellow exterior and green awning looked lovely in the wet, and somehow I felt a little lucky, thinking a rainy day in Okinawa isn't so bad after all.

Rating (9/15): Just plain tasty. All in all, the "Motobu soba three-kind platter" was "right-down-the-middle Okinawa soba" that tourists and locals alike can reach for with confidence: a clear pork-bone-based broth, softish medium-thin straight noodles, and three kinds of lightly seasoned meat. The meltingness of the soft-bone pork ribs earns high marks, while the two sinewy meats may divide opinion. Next time I'd like to have it with jushi on the side and plenty of kōrēgūsu🍜.

我那覇そば.name: Ganaha Soba
我那覇そば.desc: The "Original Soki Soba Shop" (since 1948) inside "Haneji no Eki" on National Route 58. A very Nago-style bowl: the original soki soba with three chunky pork spare ribs and a touch of color from kelp. Ticket-machine style with a wide menu.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT-4o), with some additions of my own lol
I went to eat here in November 2024😄

Today I stopped by "Haneji no Eki" in Makiya, Nago, and had Okinawa soba at "Ganaha Soba" inside it~. The sign says in big letters "Original Soki Soba Shop," which shows quite a bit of confidence✨ But "Marutaka Soba" in Nago also called itself the "original," and "Gabusoka Shokudo" writes "the true-lineage soki soba"... Nago is right in the middle of a "soki soba originator war"😂 (in a good way!)
Ganaha Soba inside Haneji no Eki
Ganaha Soba
Ganaha Soba
This is "Marutaka Soba," which also claims to be the original soki soba😄
This is the "true-lineage soki soba" (Gabusoka Shokudo main shop)
Well then, let me tell you about the all-important soba experience.
Inside, an old-fashioned diner feel coexists with the relaxed feel of a tourist facility, and it's quite comfortable ◎.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Menu posted on the shop wall
Menu set up inside and outside the shop
Menu set up inside and outside the shop
Ticket machine set up in the shop

You order by ticket machine. There were so many menu items that I hesitated a bit, but this time I chose the signature dish, the "original soki soba (¥900)"! When they call it the "original," you just can't not order it~😆

After sitting down and waiting a while, a bowl appeared with just the right amount of steam. Ooh, there are three chunky soki rolling around on top! That's impactful. Kelp and green onion add color too, and it looks really appetizing. Itadakimasu🙏
Original soki soba ¥900

First, a sip of the broth. Yep, it's a combined pork and bonito broth. But rather than one of them coming to the front, it's a balanced broth where neither stands out. No strong personality, but it was an ordinary kind of taste that would probably appeal to everyone😊
Original soki soba ¥900

The noodles are thick, flat, and straight. On the soft side. The look of it with kelp as a topping reminds me of "Miyazato Soba"😄 The kelp topping is very Nago-like too, and nice! I think people who like the Miyazato Soba style will love it👍

And the soki. Three large cuts, with a perfect presence✨ They don't quite fall apart when you put them in your mouth... some sinewy texture remains, so they're satisfying to chew. The seasoning is on the light side. But honestly, I can't deny the impression that it's a little understated in terms of feeling special~😅
Overall, it's a gentle Okinawa soba of the kind locals would want to eat every day. Rather than being aimed at tourists, it feels close to everyday life, and I had a good impression.
Rating (9/15): All in all, it was plainly tasty Okinawa soba. When you visit Haneji no Eki, why not give it a try?😊

さくら食堂.name: Sakura Shokudo
さくら食堂.desc: A community-rooted diner on the 2nd floor of the Nago Municipal Market. The famous "stamina bean sprout soba" is spicy with garlic and doubanjiang, and hugely filling. The yushi-dofu soba from my previous visit was superb too.
t: ― 2nd visit (November 2024) ―
This article was created with AI (Claude 3.7 Sonnet), with some additions of my own lol🍜✨ I ate here in November 2024😄
I'm introducing "Sakura Shokudo" in the municipal market in Gusuku, Nago😊 It's been quite a long time since I last ate here😆
Since it's a shop inside the market, you get the feeling it's a place loved by the locals.
"Sakura Shokudo" is on the 2nd floor of the Nago Municipal Market building
The entrance of "Sakura Shokudo" (2nd floor of the municipal market building)
When you enter, there's an old-fashioned diner atmosphere.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Sakura Shokudo's menu
Last time I ate the "yushi-dofu soba" and introduced it as being every bit as good as my recommended shops, and this time it's the "stamina bean sprout soba" I'd wanted to eat when I came next😄
Soba menu
À la carte menu
The famous "stamina bean sprout soba"

Looking at the menu, the words "stamina bean sprout soba," the house specialty, jumped out at me. This is the dish I'd been thinking "next time" about ever since I ate here last time, so I had no choice but to order it🔥
After a while the "stamina bean sprout soba" appeared! What first catches the eye is the amount of bean sprouts and chopped meat heaped on top of the noodles😳 That's hugely filling!
Stamina bean sprout soba, large ¥980
First, as usual, a gulp of the broth. Is it a combined bonito and pork broth? Or maybe it's agu broth. It's a delicious broth with plenty of umami😋
Stamina bean sprout soba, large ¥980
Next, the noodles. They're medium-thin and straight with a softish texture, but they suit this dish! Just plain tasty.

And what's distinctive is the toppings. The heap of bean sprouts and chopped meat is seasoned with garlic and doubanjiang, and the spicy flavor is irresistible! Eating it makes your body heat up and you start sweating💦 This is truly the stamina type! A powerful bowl, just as the name says.
I ordered the large size, but the volume was more than I imagined, and I almost gave up partway through😅 Next time I think a small size will be plenty. Even so, it'll surely be quite satisfying.

Rating (12/15): It's a shop in a community-rooted location, the municipal market in Gusuku, Nago, but the "stamina bean sprout soba" is a distinctive dish in a different league from ordinary Okinawa soba. Eating it while sweating from the spiciness seems addictive. I ate at this shop for the first time in a long while, and as expected, I recommend it. The volume is huge too, so I recommend going hungry! It's worth trying at least once😊
― 1st visit (July 2020) ―
It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," so I tried eating here in July 2020😀
Nago Municipal Market: Sakura Shokudo is on the 2nd floor
"Sakura Shokudo" is introduced in the "Nago Soba Map" as shop 10 of 41
I ordered the "yushi-dofu" that was introduced in the soba map.
Yushi-dofu soba ¥730

The agu broth, the pride of local Nago, has a strong flavor, with flat noodles. The toppings are generous too: wakame, sea lettuce (āsa), braised pork belly, and yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu)😀 Delicious.
The menu introduced the "stamina bean sprout soba" as Sakura Shokudo's specialty, so I'd like to try that next🤤
Rating (12/15): Generous and delicious. This one is also recommended, so please give it a try.
PS: There's a certain amount of free parking in the municipal parking lot, so be careful not to park at a nearby coin parking lot without checking for open spaces.
